description:
Question. TPC-H 3.0.1 clause 5.3.7.10 says that before the refresh stream the dbgen data may only be generated, permuted and relocated, and that 'data formatting or database activity' on it must be inside the refresh timing. BenchBox runs work on the refresh data before the RF timer starts, at three sites: the power test (TPCHPowerTest._execute_refresh_function in benchbox/core/tpch/power_test.py), the throughput refresh stream (benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py), and the standalone TPC-H maintenance test (_execute_rf1 and _execute_rf2 in benchbox/core/tpch/maintenance_test.py, run by official_benchmark.py and the execution mixin). At each, check_rf1_preconditions and check_rf2_preconditions (benchbox/core/tpch/refresh.py) are called before the timer starts. check_rf1_preconditions also parses orders.tbl.uN through _source_row_chunks, which is arguably 'formatting' and warms the OS page cache for the timed read. The RF2 check counts exactly the LINEITEM and ORDERS rows RF2 then deletes, which can warm the engine cache. The RF2 post-check (check_rf2_applied) runs after the timer; in the throughput test the post-checks run after all streams finish (_check_refresh_postconditions).

The pre-timer placement was deliberate ('safety checks no longer count toward Ts') and is pinned by test_throughput_runs_all_safety_checks_outside_the_refresh_measurement in tests/unit/core/tpch/test_tpch_refresh.py. The refresh stream's start and end are part of the Ts span (benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py compute_metrics), so any check placed inside the refresh stream's window changes Ts and Throughput@Size.

Open interpretation: whether those checks are 'database activity on these data' in the sense of 5.3.7.10. The spec text does not say. Decide and record it.

Options.
A. Run the checks after the RF timer. RF1: duplicate-key and row-count verification after commit. RF2: verify against the delete counts the driver reports plus the existing check_rf2_applied. In the throughput test the post-checks run after the refresh stream's end_monotonic, as the existing post-checks do; in the power test and maintenance test after the RF timer stops. A failed check leaves the database mutated, but a failed precondition already means the database must be reloaded. Spec-safe under either reading.
B. Keep the checks before the timer and record a documented deviation in docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md. Consequence, stated plainly: no run with refresh functions enabled may export QphH@Size as official, because the official eligibility rests on refresh evidence; comparability with published TPC-H results is weaker.
C. Run the checks inside the timer. Spec-safe, but [INFERENCE] about 15 scans of 1000-key IN lists at SF10 would roughly double native DuckDB RF1 time, and it adds check cost to Ts.
Recommended: A.

Evidence to prepare (agent, read-only; throwaway scripts not committed): (1) re-read 5.3.7.3 and 5.3.7.10 and quote them in the brief; (2) on DuckDB at SF1 and SF10, time the RF1 and RF2 precondition checks next to the RF1/RF2 apply calls, replacing the inference in option C with numbers; (3) whether the driver reports a deleted-row count for DELETE on each refresh-capable engine and through the connection wrappers (apply_rf2 today returns expected_orders plus a count from the pre-check and never reads rowcount), because option A's RF2 check depends on it; (4) every code path that gates official QphH eligibility on refresh evidence (benchbox/core/results/metrics.py, benchbox/core/tpch/official_benchmark.py) so option B's consequence is concrete; (5) whether any published bundle depends on the current placement.

Decision gate. Only the owner decides. An agent prepares the brief and updates dependents after the decision; it must not choose.

Guardrails: read-only until the decision is recorded; no changes to other items except the dependents named in the acceptance.
